l008-001:
Use simple mode for straightforward relaying, or advanced mode for more MediaMTX features
Switching restarts the engine and interrupts running relays for a few seconds
l008-002: Keeps only basic relaying for a cleaner UI; suited to users who just want quick forwarding
l008-003:
• Shows only the settings relaying needs
• Supports RTMP, RTSP and SRT push sources
• Supports relaying to major streaming platforms and custom targets
• Supports RTMP / RTMPS push proxies
• Cannot use features exclusive to advanced mode, but never deletes existing configuration
l008-004: Unlocks more MediaMTX features: pull sources, recording, multi-user authentication and connection tuning; suited to users who need advanced MediaMTX capabilities
l008-005:
• Every feature of simple mode
• Local recording for each input source, saved to the recording directory
• User accounts with per-source push permissions
• Pull sources that fetch IP cameras, media servers and other remote streams
• Connection tuning for RTSP transports and WebRTC handshake / track gathering timeouts, adapting to different networks
l008-008: After switching you can configure pull sources, recording, multi-user authentication and connection tuning, and the Input sources page shows recording buttons. The engine restarts once, interrupting running relays for a few seconds
l008-009: After switching, recording, multi-user authentication and connection tuning stop applying, and pull-based input sources are disabled. Existing configuration is kept. The engine restarts once, interrupting running relays for a few seconds

The proxy used when an output target follows the default setting
For example socks5://127.0.0.1:8888 or http://127.0.0.1:8888; without a scheme http is assumed
ls04-004:
Applies to RTMP / RTMPS targets only
SRT, RTSP and WebRTC carry media over UDP, which a process-level proxy cannot handle, so those stay direct even if configured
To proxy them, use a TUN-mode proxy or a process-level forwarder
